questions.question: What makes AI evaluation drift dangerous?
options: A familiar score can stop representing current production behavior.
Every evaluation run necessarily becomes slower over time.
A model must be retrained whenever traffic volume changes.
All production examples eventually become invalid JSON.
questions.explanation: System, population, evaluator, or instrumentation changes can break the meaning of a previously useful score.

questions.question: A top-line quality score falls immediately after both the judge model and product prompt changed. What should the team conclude first?
options: The movement is ambiguous until paired comparisons isolate the product and judge effects.
The product prompt is definitely responsible.
The judge model is definitely responsible.
The change can be ignored because two versions moved together.
questions.explanation: When the measured system and measurement instrument change together, the top-line delta cannot identify a cause.

questions.question: Which comparison best isolates application behavior?
options: Score baseline and candidate outputs on comparable cases with the same frozen judge.
Compare two traffic weeks using different judges.
Average every slice into one score.
Ask only the current judge whether it agrees with itself.
questions.explanation: Holding cases and the evaluator stable makes the application version the main changed variable.

questions.question: A critical language represents 3% of traffic. Why can a risk-weighted sample be preferable to a purely random sample?
options: It deliberately gathers enough cases to estimate the high-impact slice instead of letting volume determine coverage.
It makes confidence intervals unnecessary.
It turns the oversampled blend into the natural fleet average.
It guarantees every automated judgment is correct.
questions.explanation: Rare slices can receive too few random cases for a decision; risk-weighted allocation increases evidence where failure impact is high.

questions.question: The global score improves, but the lower confidence bound for a critical billing slice is below its release floor. What is the safe action?
options: Block or hold the release until the slice failure is understood and contained.
Ship because the aggregate improved.
Delete the billing cases from the suite.
Lower the floor after seeing the result.
questions.explanation: A predeclared critical-slice floor is a hard decision boundary that an aggregate improvement must not cancel.

questions.question: Which record is required to reproduce and interpret an evaluation result?
options: System, dataset, slice, sampling, judge, rubric, threshold, and decision versions.
Only the final percentage score.
Only the model provider name.
Only the dashboard screenshot.
questions.explanation: Complete identity is needed to know what changed, replay the result, and connect a failed gate to an operational response.
